title_en: Wetland Protection Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of strengthening wetland protection, maintaining wetland ecological functions and biodiversity, ensuring ecological security, promoting ecological civilization, and achieving harmonious coexistence between humans and nature.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to activities such as wetland protection, utilization, restoration, and related management activities conducted within the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under its jurisdiction.
For the purposes of this Law, "wetlands" means natural or artificial, perennial or seasonal areas of water accumulation or water bodies with significant ecological functions, including sea areas with a water depth of no more than six meters at low tide, excluding paddy fields and artificial water bodies and tidal flats used for aquaculture. The State shall implement a hierarchical management and list system for wetlands.
The protection, utilization, and related management activities of wetlands in rivers, lakes, sea areas, etc. shall also be governed by the Water Law of the People's Republic of China, the Flood Control Law of the People's Republic of China, the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People's Republic of China, the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Yangtze River Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Fisheries Law of the People's Republic of China, the Sea Area Use Management Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws.

Article 3 Wetland protection shall adhere to the principles of prioritizing protection, strict management, systematic governance, scientific restoration, and rational utilization, so as to bring into play the multiple ecological functions of wetlands, including water conservation, climate regulation, environmental improvement, and biodiversity maintenance.

Article 4 The people's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate wetland protection into the national economic and social development plans, and shall include the funds required for wetland protection work in the budgets in accordance with the principle of division of powers.
The local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for wetland protection within their respective administrative regions and shall take measures to maintain stable wetland areas and enhance wetland ecological functions.
The people's governments of townships shall organize the masses to carry out wetland protection work, and the村民 committees shall provide assistance.

Article 5 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and management of wetland resources, the formulation of wetland protection plans and relevant national standards, the supervision and management of wetland development and utilization, and wetland ecological protection and restoration. The competent departments of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, agriculture and rural affairs, and other relevant departments under the State Council shall undertake wetland protection, restoration, and management work according to their respective functions and duties.
The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall, together with the competent departments of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, agriculture and rural affairs, and other competent departments under the State Council, establish a wetland protection coordination and information notification mechanism.

Article 6 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the coordination of wetland protection. The relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for wetland protection, restoration, and management work according to their respective functions and duties.

Article 7 The people's governments at all levels shall strengthen wetland protection publicity, education, and popularization of scientific knowledge, carry out publicity and education activities through Wetland Protection Day, Wetland Protection Publicity Week, etc., and enhance the wetland protection awareness of the whole society; they shall encourage grassroots self-governing organizations, social organizations, and volunteers to carry out publicity activities on wetland protection laws, regulations, and knowledge, creating a good atmosphere for wetland protection.
Competent education authorities and schools shall focus on cultivating students' awareness of wetland protection in educational and teaching activities.
News media shall conduct public interest publicity on wetland protection laws, regulations, and knowledge, and exercise public opinion supervision over acts that damage wetlands.

Article 8 The State encourages units and individuals to participate in wetland protection activities by means of donation, funding, voluntary service, etc., in accordance with law.
Units and individuals that achieve remarkable results in wetland protection shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with relevant State regulations.

Article 9 The State supports the research, development, application, and promotion of science and technology for wetland protection, strengthens the training of professional and technical personnel for wetland protection, and improves the level of science and technology for wetland protection.
Article 10 The State supports international cooperation and exchanges in wetland protection science and technology, biodiversity, migratory bird migration, and other aspects.

Article 11 All units and individuals shall have the obligation to protect wetlands and shall have the right to report or accuse acts that damage wetlands. The organ that receives the report or accusation shall promptly handle it and protect the lawful rights and interests of the reporter or accuser according to law.

Article 12 The State shall establish a wetland resource survey and evaluation system.
The competent department of natural resources under the State Council shall, together with the competent department of forestry and grassland and other relevant departments under the State Council, periodically conduct national wetland resource survey and evaluation work, investigate wetland types, distribution, area, biodiversity, protection and utilization, etc., and establish a unified information release and sharing mechanism.

Article 13 The State shall implement a system of total wetland area control and incorporate the total wetland area control targets into the wetland protection target responsibility system.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland, and natural resources under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments under the State Council, determine the total wetland area control targets for the whole country and for each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government based on the national wetland resource situation, natural changes, and total wetland area control requirements, and submit them to the State Council for approval. Local people's governments at all levels shall take effective measures to implement the requirements of the total wetland area control targets.

Article 14 The State shall implement hierarchical management of wetlands, and shall divide wetlands into important wetlands and general wetlands according to their ecological location, area, and the importance of maintaining ecological functions and biodiversity. Important wetlands include nationally important wetlands and provincially important wetlands; wetlands other than important wetlands are general wetlands. Important wetlands shall be demarcated into the ecological protection red line according to law.
The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall, together with the competent departments of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, agriculture and rural affairs, and other relevant departments under the State Council, publish the list and scope of nationally important wetlands and establish protection signs. Internationally important wetlands shall be included in the list of nationally important wetlands.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government or their authorized departments shall be responsible for publishing the list and scope of provincially important wetlands and file them with the competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council.
The list and scope of general wetlands shall be published by the local people's governments at or above the county level or their authorized departments.

Article 15 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments under the State Council, formulate a national wetland protection plan in accordance with the national economic and social development plan, the territorial space plan, and the ecological environment protection plan, and submit it to the State Council or its authorized department for approval before organizing its implementation.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland under the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, together with the relevant departments, formulate wetland protection plans for their respective administrative regions in accordance with the territorial space plan at the corresponding level and the wetland protection plan at the next higher level, and submit them to the people's government at the same level for approval before organizing their implementation.
Wetland protection plans shall specify the objectives and tasks, overall layout, key points of protection and restoration, and safeguard measures for wetland protection. If an approved wetland protection plan needs to be adjusted, the original approval procedure shall be followed.
The formulation of wetland protection plans shall be coordinated with plans such as comprehensive river basin plans, flood control plans, etc.

Article 16 The competent departments of forestry and grassland, and standardization under the State Council shall, together with the competent departments of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, agriculture and rural affairs under the State Council, organize the formulation of national standards for wetland classification, monitoring and early warning, ecological restoration, etc.; where national standards have not been provided for, local standards may be formulated in accordance with law and filed.

Article 17 The competent departments of forestry and grassland under the people's governments at or above the county level shall establish a wetland protection expert consultation mechanism to provide evaluation and demonstration services for formulating wetland protection plans, compiling wetland lists, formulating relevant standards, etc.

Article 18 When registering the ownership of natural resources involving wetlands, the geographical coordinates, spatial scope, type, area, and other information of the wetlands shall be recorded in accordance with regulations.

Article 19 The State shall strictly control the occupation of wetlands.
It shall be prohibited to occupy nationally important wetlands, except for national major projects, disaster prevention and mitigation projects, important water conservancy and protection facility projects, wetland protection projects, etc.
The site selection and route selection of construction projects shall avoid wetlands; where avoidance is not possible, occupation shall be minimized, and necessary measures shall be taken to reduce the adverse impact on wetland ecological functions.
When the planning site selection or route selection of a construction project is subject to approval or verification and involves a nationally important wetland, the opinion of the competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall be solicited; if it involves a provincially important wetland or a general wetland, the opinion of the department authorized by the local people's government at or above the county level shall be solicited according to the management authority.

Article 20 Where a construction project indeed needs to temporarily occupy wetlands, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Water Law of the People's Republic of China, the Forest Law of the People's Republic of China, the Grassland Law of the People's Republic of China, the Sea Area Use Management Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws and regulations. The period of temporary wetland occupation generally shall not exceed two years, and no permanent buildings shall be constructed on the temporarily occupied wetlands.
Within one year after the expiration of the period of temporary wetland occupation, the land-using unit or individual shall restore the wetland area and ecological conditions.

Article 21 Except for wetlands within the river management scope and flood storage and detention areas occupied due to flood control, navigation, ports, or other water projects, a unit that has been approved to occupy important wetlands according to law shall restore or reconstruct wetlands equivalent to the area and quality of the occupied wetlands based on local natural conditions; where it is unable to restore or reconstruct, it shall pay a wetland restoration fee. If the wetland restoration fee has been paid, no other restoration fees of the same nature shall be paid.
The measures for the payment and use management of wetland restoration fees shall be formulated by the competent department of finance under the State Council together with the competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council and other relevant departments.

Article 22 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall carry out dynamic monitoring of nationally important wetlands in accordance with monitoring technical specifications, and promptly obtain information on changes in wetland distribution, area, water volume, biodiversity, threat status, etc.
The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall, based on monitoring data, assess the ecological status of nationally important wetlands and issue early warning information in accordance with regulations.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland under the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall carry out dynamic monitoring, assessment, and early warning of provincially important wetlands in accordance with monitoring technical specifications.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland under the local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen dynamic monitoring of general wetlands.

Article 23 The State shall adhere to ecological priority and green development, improve the wetland protection system, perfect the policy support and scientific and technological support mechanisms for wetland protection, ensure the ecological functions and sustainable use of wetlands, and realize the unity of ecological, social, and economic benefits.

Article 24 The people's governments at or above the provincial level and their relevant departments shall, in accordance with wetland protection plans and the needs of wetland protection, incorporate wetlands into national parks, nature reserves, or natural parks according to law.

Article 25 Local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall take measures to prevent and control the adverse impact of human activities on wetlands and their biodiversity, strengthen wetland pollution prevention and control, mitigate wetland degradation caused by human and natural factors, and maintain the stability of wetland ecological functions.
When engaging in utilization activities such as tourism, planting, livestock farming, aquaculture, and navigation within wetland areas, the natural conditions of the wetlands shall not be altered, and measures shall be taken to mitigate the adverse impact on wetland ecological functions.
When handling relevant administrative licenses such as environmental impact assessment, territorial space planning, sea area use, aquaculture, and flood control, the relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the review of the necessity, rationality, and wetland protection measures of the relevant wetland utilization activities.

Article 26 Local people's governments at all levels shall provide classified guidance on the utilization activities of provincially important wetlands and general wetlands, encourage units and individuals to carry out eco-tourism, eco-agriculture, eco-education, nature experience, and other activities that meet wetland protection requirements, and moderately control the scale of wetland utilization such as planting and aquaculture.
Local people's governments at all levels shall encourage relevant units to give priority to arranging local residents to participate in wetland management and protection.

Article 27 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall fully consider the need to ensure the ecological functions of important wetlands and optimize the industrial layout around important wetlands.
Local people's governments at or above the county level may adopt methods such as targeted support, industrial transfer, attracting social funds, and community co-construction to promote green development in areas around wetlands and promote coordination between economic development and wetland protection.

Article 29 The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, carry out monitoring of harmful organisms in wetlands and promptly take effective measures to prevent, control, and eliminate the harm of harmful organisms to the wetland ecosystem.

Article 30 The people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the protection of wetlands where national key protected wild animals and plants are concentrated. No unit or individual shall destroy the living environment of birds and aquatic organisms.
It shall be prohibited to engage in activities such as fishing, digging for benthic organisms, picking bird eggs, destroying bird nests, and other activities that endanger the survival and reproduction of water birds in nature reserves and other important habitats where water birds are the protection targets. Activities such as bird watching, scientific research, and science popularization shall maintain a safe distance to avoid affecting the normal foraging and reproduction of birds.
Protection measures shall be implemented in important habitats such as spawning grounds, feeding grounds, wintering grounds, and migration passages of important aquatic organisms. Where construction of sluices or dams on migration passages may affect the migration of aquatic organisms after approval according to law, the construction unit shall build fish passage facilities or take other remedial measures.
It shall be prohibited to introduce and release alien species into wetlands; if introduction is indeed necessary, a scientific assessment shall be conducted and approval shall be obtained according to law.

Article 31 The competent department of water administration under the State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the management and protection of wetlands within rivers and lakes, and take remediation and restoration measures such as water system connection, dredging, water conservation, and soil and water conservation according to local conditions; strictly control wetland development and utilization activities in areas such as river sources, flood storage and detention areas, and areas with severe soil erosion, so as to reduce the adverse impact on wetlands and their biodiversity.

Article 32 The competent department of natural resources under the State Council and local people's governments at all levels along the coast shall strengthen the management and protection of coastal wetlands, and strictly control the reclamation of coastal wetlands. For projects approved according to law, ecological protection and restoration shall be implemented simultaneously to mitigate the adverse impact on the ecological functions of coastal wetlands.

Article 33 The competent department of housing and urban-rural construction under the State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the management and protection of urban wetlands, take measures such as urban water system management and ecological restoration to improve the ecological quality of urban wetlands, and bring into play the functions of urban wetlands such as rainwater and flood storage, water purification, leisure and recreation, and science education.

Article 34 The local people's governments at or above the county level in the area where mangrove wetlands are located shall organize the formulation of special plans for the protection of mangrove wetlands and take effective measures to protect mangrove wetlands.
Mangrove wetlands shall be included in the list of important wetlands; those that meet the criteria for nationally important wetlands shall be given priority for inclusion in the list of nationally important wetlands.
It shall be prohibited to occupy mangrove wetlands. Where occupation is indeed necessary due to national major projects, disaster prevention and mitigation, etc., after assessment by the relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, and protection and restoration work shall be carried out. If a relevant construction project changes the hydrological regime of the estuary where mangrove wetlands are located and has a significant impact on the growth of mangroves, effective measures shall be taken to mitigate the adverse impact.
It shall be prohibited to dig ponds in mangrove wetlands; to cut, dig, transplant mangroves or excessively pick mangrove seeds; and to release or plant species that harm the growth of mangroves. Where cutting, digging, transplanting, or picking is necessary for scientific research, medicine, or mangrove wetland protection, etc., the matter shall be handled in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.

Article 35 The local people's governments at or above the county level in the area where peat bog wetlands are located shall formulate special plans for the protection of peat bog wetlands and take effective measures to protect peat bog wetlands.
Peat bog wetlands that meet the criteria for important wetlands shall be included in the list of important wetlands.
It shall be prohibited to extract peat or unauthorizedly extract groundwater from peat bog wetlands; it shall be prohibited to discharge the stored water of peat bog wetlands outward, except where necessary for disaster prevention and mitigation.

Article 36 The State shall establish a wetland ecological protection compensation system.
The State Council and the people's governments of provinces shall, in accordance with the principle of division of powers, increase financial input for the protection of important wetlands and increase the financial transfer payments to the areas where important wetlands are located.
The State encourages the people's governments of wetland ecological protection areas and wetland ecological benefit areas to carry out inter-regional ecological protection compensation through consultation or market mechanisms.
Where the lawful rights and interests of wetland owners or users are damaged due to public interests such as ecological protection, the people's governments at or above the county level shall provide compensation.

Article 37 The people's governments at or above the county level shall adhere to the principle of giving priority to natural recovery and combining natural recovery with artificial restoration, strengthen wetland restoration work, restore wetland areas, and improve the quality of wetland ecosystems.
The people's governments at or above the county level shall carry out comprehensive improvement and restoration of severely fragmented or functionally degraded natural wetlands, and give priority to restoring important wetlands with severely degraded ecological functions.

Article 38 When organizing wetland protection and restoration, the people's governments at or above the county level shall fully consider the conditions of water resources endowment and carrying capacity, rationally allocate water resources, ensure the basic ecological water demand of wetlands, and maintain the ecological functions of wetlands.

Article 39 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall conduct scientific demonstration and take measures according to local conditions to restore the ecological functions of former wetlands, degraded wetlands, salinized wetlands, etc. that have the conditions for restoration.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with wetland protection plans, take measures such as water body treatment, land consolidation, vegetation restoration, and animal protection according to local conditions to enhance the ecological functions and carbon sink functions of wetlands.
It shall be prohibited to illegally occupy farmland or other land to construct artificial wetlands.

Article 40 The local people's governments at or above the county level in the area where mangrove wetlands are located shall give priority to the restoration of mangrove wetlands in areas with important ecological functions, areas with higher risk of marine disasters, areas for the protection of endangered species, or areas with better afforestation conditions; carry out rescue restoration of severely degraded mangrove wetlands; and local tree species shall be used as much as possible in restoration.

Article 41 The local people's governments at or above the county level in the area where peat bog wetlands are located shall, according to local conditions, organize the restoration of degraded peat bog wetlands and adopt corresponding restoration measures based on the type, development status, and degree of degradation of the peat bog wetlands.

Article 42 Wetland restoration plans shall be formulated for the restoration of important wetlands.
The restoration plan for important wetlands shall be submitted to the competent department of forestry and grassland under the people's government at or above the provincial level for approval. Before approving the restoration plan, the competent department of forestry and grassland shall solicit the opinions of the departments of natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, agriculture and rural affairs, and other relevant departments under the people's government at the same level.

Article 43 The restoration of important wetlands shall be carried out in accordance with the approved wetland restoration plan.
After the restoration of important wetlands is completed, it shall pass the acceptance inspection by the competent department of forestry and grassland under the people's government at or above the provincial level, and the restoration status shall be disclosed according to law. The competent department of forestry and grassland under the people's government at or above the provincial level shall strengthen the post-restoration management and dynamic monitoring of restored wetlands, and carry out post-evaluation of restoration effects as needed.

Article 44 Where wetlands are damaged due to illegal occupation, extraction, reclamation, filling, discharge of pollutants, or other activities, the perpetrator of the illegal act shall be responsible for restoration. If the perpetrator changes, the subject that succeeds its claims and debts shall be responsible for restoration.
Where wetlands are damaged due to major natural disasters, or where the subject responsible for wetland restoration ceases to exist or cannot be determined, the people's governments at or above the county level shall organize the implementation of restoration.

Article 45 The competent departments of forestry and grassland, natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, and agriculture and rural affairs under the people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and according to their respective functions and duties, supervise and inspect activities such as the protection, restoration, and utilization of wetlands, and investigate and deal with illegal acts that damage wetlands according to law.

Article 47 Where the competent departments of forestry and grassland, natural resources, water administration, housing and urban-rural construction, ecological environment, and agriculture and rural affairs under the people's governments at or above the county level perform their supervision and inspection duties according to law, the relevant units and individuals shall cooperate and shall not refuse or obstruct.

Article 48 The competent department of forestry and grassland under the State Council shall strengthen the supervision and inspection of the protection of nationally important wetlands. The competent departments of forestry and grassland under the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall strengthen the supervision and inspection of the protection of provincially important wetlands.
The competent departments of forestry and grassland and relevant departments under the people's governments at the county level shall make full use of information technology to supervise and inspect wetland protection.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall disclose information related to wetland protection according to law and accept social supervision.

Article 49 The State shall implement a wetland protection target responsibility system and incorporate wetland protection into the comprehensive performance evaluation of local people's governments.
For areas where the problem of wetland damage is prominent, protection work is ineffective, and the masses have strong complaints, the competent department of forestry and grassland under the people's government at or above the provincial level shall, together with relevant departments, interview the principal leading persons of the people's government of that area.
Article 50 The protection, restoration, and management of wetlands shall be included in the audit of natural resource assets of leading officials upon their departure.

Article 51 Where the relevant department of a people's government at or above the county level discovers an illegal act of destroying wetlands or receives a report of an illegal act, but fails to investigate and handle it or fails to investigate and handle it according to law, or commits any other act of dereliction of duty, abuse of power, or engaging in malpractices for personal gain, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 52 Where a construction project illegally occupies a nationally important wetland in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent departments of forestry and grassland and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective functions and duties, order the cessation of the illegal act, require the demolition of newly built buildings, structures, and other facilities on the illegally occupied wetland within a prescribed time limit, and restore the wetland or take other remedial measures, and impose a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan per square meter of the illegally occupied wetland area; if the person who commits the illegal act does not cease construction or fails to demolish within the prescribed time limit, the department that made the decision on administrative penalty shall apply to a People's Court for compulsory execution according to law.

Article 53 Where a construction project occupies an important wetland but fails to restore or rebuild the wetland in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the county level shall order the restoration or reconstruction of the wetland within a prescribed time limit; if the party fails to rectify within the prescribed time limit, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the county level shall entrust another person to perform the restoration or reconstruction on its behalf, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by the person who commits the illegal act, and a fine of not less than 500 yuan but not more than 2,000 yuan per square meter of the occupied wetland area shall be imposed.

Article 54 Where a person reclaims, fills, or buries natural wetlands in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent departments of forestry and grassland and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective functions and duties, order the cessation of the illegal act, require the restoration of the wetland or the adoption of other remedial measures within a prescribed time limit, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than 500 yuan but not more than 5,000 yuan per square meter of the damaged wetland area; if the act damages a nationally important wetland, a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan per square meter of the damaged wetland area shall be imposed.
Where a person drains natural wetlands or permanently cuts off the water source of natural wetlands in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of the illegal act, require the restoration of the wetland or the adoption of other remedial measures within a prescribed time limit, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if serious consequences are caused, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be concurrently imposed.

Article 55 Where a person introduces or releases alien species into wetlands in violation of the provisions of this Law, the matter shall be handled and penalties shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Biosafety Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws and regulations.

Article 56 Where a person digs ponds in mangrove wetlands in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent departments of forestry and grassland and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective functions and duties, order the cessation of the illegal act, require the restoration of the wetland or the adoption of other remedial measures within a prescribed time limit, and impose a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan per square meter of the damaged wetland area; if trees are damaged, the person shall be ordered to replant and achieve survival of not less than one time but not more than three times the number of damaged trees within a prescribed time limit; if the number of damaged trees cannot be determined, the number of trees shall be calculated based on the growth density of the same tree species in the same area.
Where a person releases or plants species that hinder the growth of mangroves in mangrove wetlands in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of the illegal act, require the cleaning up within a prescribed time limit, and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if serious consequences are caused, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 57 Where a person extracts peat in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent departments of forestry and grassland and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, according to their respective functions and duties, order the cessation of the illegal act, require the restoration of the wetland or the adoption of other remedial measures within a prescribed time limit, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan per cubic meter of the extracted peat volume.
Where a person drains water from a peat bog wetland in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of the illegal act, require the restoration of the wetland or the adoption of other remedial measures within a prescribed time limit, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be concurrently imposed.

Article 58 Where a person restores wetlands without preparing a restoration plan or fails to restore wetlands in accordance with the restoration plan, thereby causing damage to wetlands, in violation of the provisions of this Law, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan.

Article 59 Where a person who commits an illegal act of destroying wetlands fails to restore the wetlands within the prescribed time limit or in accordance with the restoration plan, the competent department of forestry and grassland of the people's government at or above the county level shall entrust another person to perform the restoration on its behalf, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by the person who commits the illegal act; if the person who commits the illegal act loses the ability to restore due to being declared bankrupt or for other reasons, the people's government at or above the county level shall organize the restoration.

Article 60 Where a person refuses or obstructs the supervision and inspection carried out according to law by the relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level in violation of the provisions of this Law, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the person may be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification.

Article 61 Where a person causes damage to the ecological environment in violation of the provisions of this Law, the authority designated by the State or the organization prescribed by law shall have the right to request, according to law, the person who commits the illegal act to assume the liability for restoration, pay compensation for losses, and bear relevant expenses.

Article 62 Where a violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security administration penalty according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 64 The provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and cities divided into districts and autonomous prefectures may, based on their local conditions, formulate specific measures for wetland protection.
Article 65 This Law shall come into force as of June 1, 2022.
